categories.main_business_segments: Kilroy Realty Corporation operates primarily in one business segment: ownership, development, acquisition, and management of Class A office, life science, and mixed-use properties. The company’s stabilized portfolio consists mainly of office and life science properties, with a smaller component of residential and retail assets.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: KRC’s core methods center on real estate development, redevelopment, and property management, with a focus on sustainable building practices. The company integrates advanced building management systems, security operation centers, and tenant experience solutions, and constructs new developments to LEED Platinum or Gold standards, emphasizing energy efficiency and environmental sustainability.
categories.primary_customers_markets: KRC’s primary customers are tenants in the technology, life science, healthcare, media, finance, insurance, real estate, and professional services industries. The tenant base is concentrated in knowledge and creative sectors, with technology tenants accounting for 56% of annualized base rent, followed by life science/healthcare (17%), media (10%), and others.
categories.geographic_coverage: KRC’s operations are concentrated on the U.S. West Coast, specifically Greater Los Angeles, San Diego County, the San Francisco Bay Area, and Greater Seattle, with recent expansion into Austin, Texas. As of December 31, 2021, nearly all properties and projects are located in California, Washington, and Texas.
categories.supply_chain_position: KRC operates as a downstream participant in the real estate supply chain, serving as a landlord and property manager directly interfacing with end-user tenants. The company does not engage in construction contracting or material supply but oversees development, redevelopment, and ongoing management of completed properties.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, KRC prioritizes long-term sustainable growth in net operating income and funds from operations through active development, redevelopment, and capital recycling. The company emphasizes sustainability leadership, aiming for carbon-neutral operations, LEED certifications, and tenant-focused green initiatives, while expanding into new markets and product types such as life science and mixed-use developments.
categories.revenue_model: KRC generates revenue primarily through rental income from leasing office, life science, residential, and retail space to tenants. Lease structures include full service gross, modified gross, and triple net leases, with additional income from tenant reimbursements, parking, and occasional property sales or capital recycling transactions.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: KRC competes with other developers, owners, and operators of office, life science, and mixed-use real estate, including both public and private REITs and institutional investors. The company positions itself as a premier provider of high-quality, sustainable properties in supply-constrained, innovation-driven markets, often outperforming peers in sustainability rankings and tenant experience.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2021, KRC had total assets of approximately $10.6 billion and a stabilized portfolio of 120 office/life science buildings totaling over 15.4 million square feet. The company reported net income of $658.9 million and funds from operations of $462.3 million for 2021, with a moderate leverage profile (34.4% debt to total market capitalization) and a history of steady growth through development and acquisitions.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: KRC differentiates itself through its focus on Class A, sustainable, and amenity-rich properties in high-barrier, innovation-centric markets. The company’s leadership in sustainability (carbon-neutral operations, LEED/ENERGY STAR certifications), tenant experience, and ability to deliver modern, collaborative workspaces provide a compelling value proposition for leading technology, life science, and creative tenants.
